summary: On node1 (RHEL 7.9), created a filesystem-enforced 100MB quota for datauser under /srv/data using an XFS loopback filesystem with usrquota. Verified enforcement before and after a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: RHEL 7.9, root fs is XFS mounted noquota, /srv/data did not exist, xfsprogs present but no local yum repos
Created /srv/data, built a 600MB loopback file /root/srv-data.img, formatted it XFS
Mounted the image at /srv/data with 'loop,uquota' and added a persistent /etc/fstab entry
Created system account datauser (no login shell)
Set XFS user quota via xfs_quota: datauser bsoft=100m bhard=100m on /srv/data
Verified enforcement: datauser dd write stopped at exactly 104857600 bytes with 'Disk quota exceeded'
Cleaned up test file, confirmed quota report shows 0 used, 100M soft/hard
Captured baseline boot_id and quota/mount state on node1
Rebooted node1 via 'shutdown -r now' (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec was available again
Confirmed boot_id changed (0571f4dd... -> eae68577...), proving an actual restart
Confirmed /srv/data auto-remounted with usrquota and 100M limits intact post-reboot
Re-ran the 150MB write test post-reboot: enforcement still triggers 'Disk quota exceeded' at 100MB
Cleaned up post-reboot test file, final quota report shows 0 used / 100M soft+hard

evidence.requirement: datauser limited to 100MB under /srv/data, enforced by the filesystem
evidence.summary: Created XFS loopback filesystem mounted at /srv/data with usrquota, set datauser bsoft=bhard=100m via xfs_quota, and proved enforcement: dd write of 150MB stopped at exactly 104857600 bytes (100MB) with 'Disk quota exceeded'.

evidence.requirement: Quota configuration persists (fstab, not just current mount)
evidence.summary: Added /etc/fstab entry for the loopback image with loop,uquota options; verified umount+mount using only the fstab entry succeeds and preserves usrquota.
Captured boot_id 0571f4dd-60b7-4601-9295-e4eebe622784 and confirmed /srv/data mounted with usrquota and datauser's 100M soft/hard limits in place prior to reboot.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' which acknowledged before disconnecting the session; subsequent polls timed out during reboot; node1 became reachable again with new boot_id eae68577-3566-4ef3-9d8d-87a95715d3f6, proving an actual restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of required service/data (quota enforcement)
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/data auto-mounted via fstab with usrquota and datauser's 100M limits intact; re-ran the 150MB write test and confirmed the filesystem again halted the write at exactly 100MB with 'Disk quota exceeded', then cleaned up leaving 0 bytes used.
